rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أورثنا takes two objects: in 7:137, القوم is the first and مشارق الأرض the second; similarly, أرضهم and ديارهم are respectively first and second in 33:27.
rows.anchor: فعل (أورثنا) ينصب مفعولين وعليه فإن (القوم) مفعول به أوّل و (مشارقَ) مفعول به ثاني لفعل أورثنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatʿ may affect adjectives and coordinated nouns, shifting a word from the expected case to another; the author illustrates this with the accusative form المقيمين.
rows.anchor: القطع يكون في النعوت وفي المتعاطفات. يُقطع مع المرفوع منصوب أو هذا منصوب فيأتي بصيغة مرفوعة أو منصوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative interruption singles out المقيمين الصلاة for special praise: prayer is the highest act of worship; the other coordinated descriptions remain nominative.
rows.anchor: القطع في العطف يُقطع الأمر المهم في المدح وهي تدلّ على أن الأمر المقطوع هو أمدح أو أخصّ وفي الآية التي بين أيدينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies al-muṭahharūn as angels, noting that this form is used in the Quran only for angels.
rows.anchor: أن المطهّرون هم الملائكة لأنه لم ترد في القرآن كلمة المطهرين لغير الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المطهّر is a passive participle: purified by God; forms such as المتطهرين or المطهّرين describe people who purify themselves.
rows.anchor: المُطهّر اسم مفعول وهي تعني مُطهّر من قِبَل الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angelic referent strengthens the view that the guarded book is the preserved tablet, rather than the Quran as available to people.
rows.anchor: هذا المعنى يقوّي القول أن المقصود في الآية الكتاب المكنون الذي هو في اللوح المحفوظ وليس القرآن الذي بين أيدينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because يمسّه is indicative, لا is grammatically negative, not prohibitive; a prohibitive لا would require a jussive form.
rows.anchor: طالما أن الآية جاءت بالفعل يمسُّه مرفوعاً فهذا دليل على أن (لا) نافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the verse to the rebuttal of claims that devils brought the Quran: 26:210–211 denies that, and 56:79 says they cannot reach it.
rows.anchor: فردّ الله تعالى عليهم في قوله (وَمَا تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّيَاطِينُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta-Ha narrates God's address to Moses directly and gives him worship and guidance, unlike Naml and Qasas; therefore “I am your Lord” suits Ta-Ha's direct address.
rows.anchor: في حين كان الكلام في سورة طه بصورة الخطاب. فناسب أن يقول له في طه: "أنا ربّك" بخلاف ما في النمل والقصص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct command “Throw your staff” in Naml is a direct divine utterance and marks honor; the أن construction in Qasas reports the meaning of the call, not necessarily its exact words.
rows.anchor: فقوله: "وأَلْقِ عَصاك" قول مباشر من رب العزة، وهو دال على التكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas adds أقبل because its fuller narrative and pervasive atmosphere of fear call Moses to approach as well as to stop fearing; Naml's concise context omits it.
rows.anchor: منها: أن مقام الإيجاز في النمل يستدعي عدم الإطالة بخلاف مقام التفصيل في القصص.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas is a scene of fear, so Moses is reassured that he is among the safe; Naml instead gives the general assurance that messengers do not fear in God's presence.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن المقام في سورة القصص مقام الخوف، والخائف يحتاج إلى الأمن فأمنه قائلا: "إنّكَ مِنَ الآمِنينَ"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual address to the two groups means humanity and jinn collectively; the plural command applies to every individual in both groups, as in the cited examples of two parties or disputants.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للثقلين بالمثنى هو للفريقين عموماً وهما فريقان اثنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the human is singled out because he received the revealed book and explains it to both groups; البيان is the ability to express what is within oneself.
rows.anchor: الإنسان هو الذي أُنزل عليه الكتاب أو القرآن وبيّنه للثقلين. وعلّمه البيان بمعنى ليبيّن عن نفسه

words: ليس البر بأن تأتوا البيوت من ظهورها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 2:177 البرّ is accusative as the predicate of ليس and أن تولوا is its subject; in 2:189 البرُّ is nominative as the subject of ليس.
rows.anchor: البرَّ بالفتحة في الآية الأولى هي خبر ليس و" أن تولوا " هو الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the lām, مخلَصين are people God has chosen for worship; with kasra, مخلِصين are people who make themselves sincere in worship.
rows.anchor: المخلَصين بفتح اللام تعني من أخلصه الله لعبادته وطاعته، أما المخلِصين بكسر اللام فتعني من أخلص نفسه لعبادة الله وطاعته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam as God's religion extends from the earliest prophets to the end; the Quran calls earlier prophets and their followers Muslims, while the author says Islam as the name of this religion is associated with Muhammad, its first adherent.
rows.anchor: الإسلام هو دين الله وهو الدين من أول الأنبياء إلى يوم الدين وقد سبق في القرآن الكريم ذكر نوح وإبراهيم ولوط ومن اتبعهم بأنهم من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Prophet God's servant rather than His messenger or Muhammad affirms that even the greatest human remains a servant and prevents the excess elevation Christians gave Jesus.
rows.anchor: أولها: أن الإنسان مهما عظُم لا يعدو أن يكون عبداً لله تعالى لا ينبغي لأحد أن يدّعي مقاماً ليس للآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes compulsory servitude, which every creature has whether willing or not, from chosen servitude, the highest station of the righteous.
rows.anchor: والعبودية نوعان: قسرية واختيارية، فالعبودية القسرية تتحقق شاء أم أبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts Moses being named at the theophany and his swoon with the Prophet's honored description as God's servant; he says Moses is not called “Our servant” as he falls unconscious.
rows.anchor: لم يكن ليقل خرّ عبدنا موسى أو جاء عبدنا موسى فلا يجوز أن ينسب العبودية له ثم يخرّ صعقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The designation بعبده is an added honor because it precedes the Prophet's ascent to heaven and Sidrat al-Muntaha; the bāʾ also signals divine care and protection.
rows.anchor: فلذا كان استعمال كلمة (بعبده) دلالة على زيادة التشريف له - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والباء أيضاً إضافة تشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite names al-Aziz and al-Hakim suit Pharaoh's arrogant claim to might; the definite article presents God's attributes as complete and exclusive, unlike indefinite forms that others may share.
rows.anchor: فهو المتصف بهذين الوصفين على جهة الكمال حصرا. وفي تعريف هذين الاسمين بالألف واللام من الدلالة على الكمال والحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts Naml's mention of God as al-Aziz, with no request for a brother to strengthen Moses, and the account in which Moses asks that Aaron be his supporting helper.
rows.anchor: ولما لم يقل ذلك ذكر أنه سأل ربه أن يكون له ردءا، يصدقه ويقويه وهو أخوه هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Qasas says “Lord of the worlds,” Naml also says it and then adds “the Mighty, the Wise”; this clarifies the difference between the two settings.
rows.anchor: وقد قال ذلك أيضا في النمل، فقد قال: "وسبحان الله ربّ العالمين" وزاد عليه: "إنّهُ أنا الله العَزيزُ الحَكيمُ"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta-Ha uses particular lordship because God first addresses and instructs Moses, commanding worship and prayer, then promises signs and recalls His favor; Naml and Qasas say “Lord of the worlds.”
rows.anchor: في سورة طه كان الخطاب والتوجيه لموسى عليه السلام أولا فعلمه وأرشده فقال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive يا بني expresses endearment; Luqman begins gently rather than with rebuke or scolding.
rows.anchor: كلمة تصغير للتحبيب، أي ابدأ بالكلام اللين اللطيف الهين للابن وليس بالتعنيف والزجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gentle word opens a child's heart and makes the child receptive; the author connects this approach to God's instruction that Moses and Aaron speak gently to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: الكلمة الطيبة الهينة اللينة تفتح القلوب المقفلة وتلين النفوس العصية، عكس الكلمة الشديدة المنفرة التي تقفل النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sitting beside a child, placing a hand on his head or shoulder, and addressing him tenderly can affect him more than a long explanation and remove barriers to listening.
rows.anchor: وأنت أيها الأب إن أجلست ولدك إلى جانبك ووضعت يدك على رأسه وكتفه، وقلت له يا بني، فتأكد أن هذه الكلمة بل هذه الحركة من المسح تؤثر أضعاف الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author recommends gentle, non-coercive parenting because a soft word can achieve more than a harsh one; he recounts telling his own son that gentleness had earned him more than his due.
rows.anchor: تعلمت أنه بالكلمة الهينة اللينة آخذ أكثر من حقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual رسولَا in Ta-Ha fits its dual-centered context; the singular رسول in Shu'ara and Zukhruf fits their singular-centered passages, although Shu'ara begins with a dual address before shifting to singular.
rows.anchor: المسألة تتعلق بالسياق ففي سورة طه السياق كله مبني على التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسول can have singular or plural reference, like بشر, طفل, and ضيف; the author cites Quranic uses of those forms.
rows.anchor: وكلمة (رسول) في اللغة تأتي مفرد وتأتي جمع مثل كلمة "بشر"

words: فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Al-Qari'ah's Resurrection scene is more terrifying: it repeatedly names and magnifies the calamity, while identifying the Ma'arij day with Resurrection is disputed and, on that reading, only its duration and angelic ascent are described.
rows.anchor: وليس متفقاً على تفسير أن المراد بهذا اليوم، هو اليوم الآخر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains as fluffed wool in Al-Qari'ah are more dreadful than mountains merely like wool in Ma'arij; repeated striking suggests carding and fluffing, whereas an unrepelled weight falling on wool would not.
rows.anchor: وكونها كالعهن المنفوش أعظم وأهول من أن تكون كالعهن من غير نفش كما هو ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qari'ah's expanded, detailed description suits added detail; Ma'arij is more concise, mentioning only a day whose length is fifty thousand years.
rows.anchor: التوسع والتفصيل في ذكر القارعة حسَّن ذكر الزيادة والتفصيل فيها، بخلاف الإجمال في سورة المعارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse endings suit each other: المبثوث and المنفوش rhyme in Al-Qari'ah, while المهل and العهن suit one another in Ma'arij.
rows.anchor: فناسبت كلمة (المنفوش) كلمةَ (المبثوث)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'arij depicts the sinner wishing to ransom himself from punishment with his sons, spouse, brother, clan, and everyone on earth; the scene is one of attempted ransom.
rows.anchor: أما في سورة المعارج فالمشهد مشهد فِداء وذَكَر القرابات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people are created anxious and panic at punishment, the sinner begins with his nearest kin; starting with sons shows the punishment exceeds imagination and that they are his dearest possession.
rows.anchor: إذا رأى مشهد العذاب أدركه الهلع فبدأ بالأقرب وهذا يوحي أن العذاب فوق ما يتصور الإنسان فافتدى بأعزّ ما يملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage omits parents because God commanded kindness to them and they have an exalted status; the author says one might flee from them, but could not ransom oneself by consigning them to Hell.
rows.anchor: لم يذكر في الآية الافتداء بالأم أو الأب لأن الله تعالى أمر بالإحسان إليهما ودلّ على عظيم مكانة الأبوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added أن in the Ankabut account suits its fuller, more emphatic narrative; Hud omits it in its shorter account of the messengers' arrival to Lot.
rows.anchor: أولاً لأن القصة في العنكبوت جاءت مفصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ankabut lists Lot's people's specific sins—sex with men, cutting off the road, and evil in their gatherings—whereas Hud only summarizes their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: وذكر تعالى من صفات قوم لوط السيئة (وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's distress and anticipation of rescue are greater in Ankabut: his people demand punishment and he prays for help, so he experiences the messengers' arrival as prolonged; this also makes أن apt, possibly as emphasis.
rows.anchor: برِم لوط وضيقه بقومه كان أكثر فكأنه استبطأ مجيء العذاب على هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn precede humans in some passages because their creation came first; the author cites the prior creation of jinn and Iblis's existence before Adam.
rows.anchor: لأن الجن وجودهم أسبق من الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn come first in the challenge to pass beyond the heavens because they are more capable of doing so and had been listening in on the heavens; the address begins with the stronger group.
rows.anchor: قدم الجن على الإنس لأن الجن أقدر على النفاذ من الإنسان وهم كانوا يستمعون، فلما تحداهم بالنفاذ بدأ بمن هو أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the description of Paradise women, humans are named before jinn because human intercourse would more readily repel a prospective husband; mentioning it first heightens the emphasis on their purity.
rows.anchor: نفسياً إذا كان أحدهم يريد أن يتزوج امرأة وعلِم أنه اتصل بها رجل سابق يحجم عن الزواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author glosses ṭamth as intercourse and identifies the women as the women of Paradise, including the houris; he links their being virgins to 56:36.
rows.anchor: والطمث يعني الدخول بها. الآية تتكلم عن نساء الجنة، عن حور الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from singular/third-person wording to first-person plural in فأخرجنا is iltifāt, a device used to refresh the listener's attention; the Quran uses shifts among person and number frequently.
rows.anchor: يلتفت من الغائب إلى الحاضر ومن الجمع إلى الإفراد ومن الغائب إلى المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author defines جيوبهن as the openings at the chest.
rows.anchor: الجيب هو فتحة الصدر
